notes:
SEC1 verdict: Maintainer risk: medium — Six findings. Two are protocol correctness issues (properties dropped in Chat/get; filter/sort dropped in Chat/queryChanges) that are also maintainer risk because the copy-paste pattern will propagate. Two are structural duplication issues (SetError defined twice; CHAT_READONLY not compiler-enforced) that will cause silent drift as the codebase grows. One is a silent failure mode in production code (destroy_object error discarded). One is an API surface documentation gap for ClosureHandler. No unsafe escalation in production code paths. The delegation pattern introduced for */changes is the right direction and should be extended to */get, */query, and */queryChanges as well.
SEC7 confidence: 8% chance of missed correctness bug. The 3 'GOOD' decision records and 2 confirmed bugs (JMAP-63k.17/19) were all caught. The correctness findings (RFC violations in .21/.22, CHAT_READONLY drift risk in .25, silent data corruption in .17/.19) are well-characterized with file/line citations. The performance findings (.4/.9/.12) are real but low severity. The remaining open chores (.2/.5/.8/.14/.16/.18/.20/.24) all have engineering substance. Four issues were labeled opinion (pure style: .7/.10/.11/.15). Residual risk: a concurrent-access race in the post-create dedup (already partially caught in .17/.19/.23) could have a third form — the fetch on line 448 is not atomic with the create_object call, and no issue addresses whether the backend serializes creates. Also no issue covers whether the JMAP-63k.1 'min id wins' rule is safe if two requests see different sets of duplicates (network partition). These are speculative and not obviously present in the code; their absence from findings is not alarming.
title: Review round 1: JMAP-39s production readiness
